name: Fallen Star level completeness scale
reference_game: chrono-bell (Fallen Star flagship demo, dist/demos/chrono-bell.project.json, repo base 2026-11-09)
formula: score = sum over components of weight * min(1, counted_value / reference). reference = the value measured on Fallen Star with the same counting rules, so Fallen Star = 100 and an empty project = 0. A component is capped at its weight: more than Fallen Star adds nothing.
anti_gaming: maps count only when reachable from the start map (transfer or ending continueTo), at least 100 cells, at least 6 distinct tile ids, at least one event with a command, and a tile layout that no already counted map has
events count once per content hash (id, name, position and graphic stripped) and only with at least one command, on a counted map
dialogue counts once per normalized line (digits, spaces and punctuation removed, at least 3 chars): 'ok 1' and 'ok 2' are one line

enemies, skills, items+equipment count only when reached from a counted event, common event, quest, ending or system field, differ from the engine baseline entry, and have a distinct stat block (id, name, description, graphic ignored)
act_structure is the longest chain of counted events linked by switch or variable set -> required; it cannot be raised without real events that really set and read the flags

components.reason: World size is the first thing that separates a one-map game from Fallen Star. Counted under the reachability and distinct-layout rules so empty or cloned maps are worth 0.
Events are the authored interactions. Same weight as maps because maps without events are scenery.
Distinct dialogue lines are the cheapest honest proxy for story volume; deduplicated so repeated lines do not count.
Distinct reachable enemies show combat variety beyond the bundled slime-level defaults.
Distinct reachable skills show combat depth; lower weight than enemies because skills are often generated in batches.
Distinct reachable items and equipment (changed from the engine baseline) show an economy and progression.
Quests with at least two distinct steps are the unit of side content; uniquely titled only.
Quest steps measure quest depth, so a many-quest game of one-step quests does not saturate.
Fallen Star Act 1 has one authored ending; the scale only asks for a reachable authored ending, so its weight is small. Real endings need the play check.
Distinct BGM tracks actually used (maps, events, battle, ending, opening) excluding the engine defaults; mood variety.
Authored cutscene events plus an authored opening: directed scenes separate a story game from a walking game.
Distinct named speakers; a populated world versus two talking heads.
Distinct tilesets plus distinct map roles; a game of one repeated look scores low.
Longest switch chain between counted events: the closest measurable stand-in for acts, locks and unlocks. Weighted high because it needs genuinely connected events.
